summary: Frame successful HTTP JSON with its existing serialized payload on the handler worker

replay.detail: No startup or projection replay changes.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema version or persisted format changes.

rules.detail: No claim, admission, signature, snapshot or replication rules change.

compatibility.detail: Envelope fields and decoded JSON values stay the same. Successful payloads retain their original whitespace, escapes, duplicate keys and number spelling instead of a Value parse and re-encoding. Error normalization stays unchanged. JSON validation keeps the existing number, UTF-8 and nesting checks. Existing request deadlines and handler reader admission remain in force; dropping a request directly ends its pending post-handler body collection. The existing total request deadline still covers both handler and envelope, including refusal of late success. The same handler worker remains occupied through body collection and framing; worker/request CPU now includes that phase, while handler duration still excludes it and envelope wall time/bytes measure the completed framing phase.

downtime.detail: Only the normal binary restart is needed; no additional migration. Production latency has not been qualified.

manual.detail: No manual store repair or coordinated fleet upgrade.

recovery.detail: Older binaries read the unchanged store; rollback needs no migration.
